column3: “It had writing on both sides” renders “written inside and on [the] back.”
“Mighty” renders ἰσχυρὸν; BSB puts “break the seals” before “open the scroll.”
BSB follows the critical text with no “and to read.” “Began to weep bitterly” renders “was weeping much.”
BSB follows the critical text with “to open the scroll and its seven seals.” “Has triumphed” renders “has overcome.”
BSB follows the critical text with no “and behold.” “Encircled by” recasts “in the midst of the four living creatures”; “represent” renders “are.”
BSB adds “the scroll,” which the Textus Receptus has.
BSB follows the critical text with “those” and no “us.” “They sang” renders the present “they are singing.”
BSB follows the critical text with “them,” “a kingdom,” and “they will reign.” “To serve” is added.
“The voices of many angels and living creatures and elders encircling the throne” recasts “a voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders.”
“Praise” renders εὐλογία (“blessing”); BSB leaves out “Amen” at the end.
BSB follows the critical text with “the elders fell down and worshiped”; the Textus Receptus adds “twenty-four” and “Him who lives forever and ever.”
